Revise a student's working-knowledge document for [subtopic], in the light of an interview for a course at the [skill_level] level.

This document is shared by every course the student takes in this subtopic, at every level. It is what they know, not what one course covered.

What the document says today:

[prior_wk_doc]

The interview:

[interview_transcript]

Output the complete revised document — it replaces the old one, so anything you leave out is forgotten. Use exactly three sections, in this order: `## Solid`, `## Shaky`, `## Gaps`.

- **Solid** — what they demonstrated unaided. Only what the transcript actually shows; a claim they made about themselves is not evidence.
- **Shaky** — what they half-have: right answer by the wrong route, right idea with the wrong vocabulary, or correct in one framing and lost in another. Confident wrong answers belong here, named as such.
- **Gaps** — what did not come up or came up empty. Say which gaps matter for this course and which are simply out of scope.

Carry the existing document forward:

- **Keep every claim the interview did not touch, in its existing wording.** The interview asked about a slice of the subtopic; silence on the rest is not evidence against it.
- **Move a claim only on evidence.** Something recorded as solid that they fumbled moves down, with a note on what revealed it. Something recorded as a gap that they handled moves up.
- **A gap the new course will address stays a gap** until they show otherwise.

Use bullets. One claim per bullet, written so a later lesson can act on it. Quote the student where a quote is more precise than a paraphrase. Do not pad a section to make it look balanced — an empty section says something true.

This document is read by the model that plans and teaches the course. Write it for that reader, not for the student.
